jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer II, Agentic Apps
jobs.description:
Kit https://kit.com/ is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.

More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.

We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

THE ROLE

Creators use Kit's first-party apps and integrations https://kit.com/apps to connect Kit to the rest of their business. Today we build and maintain these apps by hand, with help from an agency partner. That doesn't scale. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer II to own app delivery and maintenance end to end, so a small team can support creators of every size.

You'll be the first engineer on the Apps squad. Your focus is shipping high quality apps at a high pace, and maintaining them to an industry-best standard. To get there, you'll take a systems-level view and build on Kit's coding agent. You'll work closely with our AI Developer Experience squad, which builds the coding agent. You'll own the creator experience of every app you build, and you're free to improve Kit's platform when that makes those apps better.

This is a full-time IC role for an AI-first, product-minded, full-stack engineer who has shipped agent workflows to production and judges them by reliable outcomes, not lines of code. You combine technical depth with leadership and extreme ownership. You take input from Partnerships, Product, and Design to help shape the "what," and you own the "how." You thrive in ambiguity, take initiative without waiting for permission, and elevate everyone around you through your generosity and optimism.

We're excited about first-party apps because they let creators do more with Kit than Kit does on its own. Our own apps should just work, and set the bar for every app built on Kit.

YOUR SUPPORT SYSTEM

You'll report to John Bohannon https://www.linkedin.com/in/imjohnbo/, Senior Engineering Manager for the Ecosystem and Apps squads. You'll collaborate closely with a Partnerships Manager, Product Manager, Product Designer, and engineers on the Ecosystem squad. You'll also work closely with our AI Developer Experience squad on Kit's coding agent, and with a contractor who helps maintain our apps.

The Apps squad works as a sibling to Ecosystem. You'll set its rhythms, collaborate with our Partnerships Manager on which apps to build next, and join Ecosystem's cycle planning.

A peer onboarding buddy will help you learn our systems and codebase, and you'll have engineers across Kit for support and mentorship.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- First Week: Set up your local environment and merge your first production code. Meet the team through Get To Know You's. Start the app handover with the contractor who maintains them today. Watch the recorded app walkthroughs and read the runbooks for our most-used apps.

- First Month: Audit our first-party apps and integrations, starting with the apps that need the most maintenance. Measure what each app costs to maintain, including partner app reviews like those at Google, Meta, and Shopify. Learn how Kit's API, OAuth, and App Store support creators from small to large. Fix bugs and support escalations in the apps you now own. Learn how Kit's coding agent works with the AI Developer Experience squad.

- First Three Months: Adapt Kit's coding agent to build your first apps and maintain existing ones. Give it the context, guardrails, and evals it needs. Turn what you learn into shared pieces every app can use, like a reusable load test, infrastructure automation, and app manifests. Write runbooks that let others work on any app. Drive each app's maintenance toward zero human time with the coding agent.

- First Six Months: Ship new apps at a steady pace. Take over the rest of the app catalog and apply the coding agent to its maintenance. Show that one engineer with agents can maintain many apps at high quality. Define the metrics and dashboards for agent-built apps: launches, reliability, time to fix, and revenue impact. Share how agents build and maintain our apps, for example in a Lunch & Learn.

- First Year: Kit ships more high-quality apps, faster, and the coding agent handles more of the routine builds and fixes, with you steering the system. The legacy integration model is retired. You use catalog metrics to recommend where the Apps squad invests next. You and the AI Developer Experience squad improve the coding agent together, so other Kit engineers benefit too.

WHAT WILL S.E.T. YOU UP FOR SUCCESS

Skills

- Expert in agentic AI development. You've built agent workflows that ship and maintain production code, with evals, guardrails, and human review.

- Create responsive and high-quality user interfaces using React and Next.js.

- Contribute to architectural decisions and continuously improve system scalability, observability, and operational excellence.

You will own features end-to-end—from PostgreSQL schema design and backend services to React/Next.js interfaces and production observability.

jobs.title: ANALISTA DESENVOLVEDOR SENIOR
jobs.description:
A Funcional Health Tech é movida pela certeza de que a Saúde é o pilar principal da vida das pessoas, por isso quebramos barreiras para promovê-la de forma sustentável.
Para realizar nosso propósito, inovamos todos os dias unindo pessoas, tecnologia e dados para prover o ecossistema da saúde com soluções que geram eficiência e sustentabilidade em toda a cadeia.
Aqui, você irá participar, de maneira direta ou indireta, da criação de novas soluções para os mais diversos serviços de saúde porque essa é a missão diária de todos nós na Funcional. Pesquisamos, criamos e fazemos acontecer, porque está em nosso DNA.
Sua missão como Desenvolvedor Sênior, será:

- Desenvolver e evoluir aplicações Full Stack, atuando no backend, frontend e integrações.

- Participar da definição de arquitetura, padrões e decisões técnicas dos projetos.

- Construir aplicações utilizando , React e .NET/C#.

- Desenvolver APIs RESTful, microsserviços e integrações entre sistemas.

- Construir soluções utilizando Inteligência Artificial e IA Generativa, incorporando recursos de IA aos produtos e processos.

We help ambitious students gain admission to the world's top universities through expert-led guidance and proven, data-driven strategies. We're backed by leading VC firms, recently closed a USD $40M Series D at a USD $640M valuation, and operate across 28 markets worldwide.
The Role
Crimson is replacing Salesforce with Salesflow, an AI-native CRM we build in-house. It runs the whole sales journey: lead intake, meeting scheduling, call transcription analysis, AI-drafted appraisals, contracts and e-signature, and invoicing. It is live for our US sales team today and rolls out to every other market over the coming months.
Our team is small and builder-heavy, and the rate of growth has made it hard to keep the underlying infrastructure and logic clean and tidy. As examples, CI checks things that have been fully deprecated, newly added modules do not always take into account legacy compatibility, and bug fixes are sometimes too narrow in scope, fixing the place the problem was seen and not the underlying cause. Compounding the above is that the code itself is for the most part written by AI – this is what enabled us to build a fully working CRM in a matter of months, but is what makes it very easy to inadvertently cross wires during development.
We are looking for the person who fixes this: you will own the backend view of the system as a whole and maintain the code that glues everything together. That means a system inventory and state transition models, CI that tests only what is needed and does that well, shared guarded entrypoints in place of multiple writers with inconsistent guards, and clear definitions for what is the source of truth when fields are shared among multiple synced systems. Salesflow is live and people depend on it every day, so this is done in steps while it runs: there is no rewrite. This is not a hands-off design role: you will be expected to push code as well as design.
In addition to the above, you'll also help to unblock users – the support team funnel tickets that prevent a user from working and require a backend code change to the dev team, most of whom are not in US time zones. You will join the team and cover the US working day, when the other members are offline.
We fully expect you to use AI to augment your analyses and write code for you but absolutely require that you have the experience to read and write code yourself, and that you know how to use AI to write code (e.g., which questions to ask, what to check, how to build internal memory structures).
What are the main responsibilities for this role?
Your top priority is to build and maintain the view of the CRM as a whole: inventory all functions, edge functions, flows, and integrations with outside systems; build the state transition map and the set of business rules the system is held to; and then ensure that architecture and CI align to this. In practice this can be split into:

- setting up a live and auto-updating inventory and model: the repo has multiple pushes every day; no-one should try updating a model by hand

- coordinating with team members on business rules: the team has, collectively, all the info; your job is to organize it and embed it in the checks

- after the above two, move into implementation: resolve technical debt caused by rapid organic growth without consistent pruning, and set up the infrastructure such that future growth automatically falls into the correct path and does not create new debt.

Aside from this, you will assist in unblocking users during US daytime hours: addressing current bugs will help you gain insight into the system as a whole, informing the main priority.

- Your first 14 days: inventory and build a model of the system; integrate into the ticket queue

- Your first 28 days: start shipping basic sanitation: clean CI and updated CLAUDE.md files (the instructions our AI agents read) so future pushes don't create more problems

- Your first 3 months: the worst of the debt is cleared and guardrails are in place, so a bug that has been fixed does not come back; your time will transition over to building new features

What skills and experience are required?
You think in systems. Shown a new product, you look for the states, the transitions and the rules that must always hold before you look at the code. You can draw how it works on one page, and you can predict from that drawing where it will break.
You learn fast and you know how you learn. You will be dropped into a large codebase you did not write. We care much more about how quickly you build an accurate picture of something unfamiliar, and how you change that picture when a fact contradicts it, than about which frameworks you already know.
You have done this before, hands-on. You have owned something that had to be right: a ledger, a billing system, an order or contract lifecycle, a reconciliation between two systems that disagreed. You ran it in production, you can tell us what went wrong with it, and you can tell us what you changed so it could not go wrong again. Being sharp is not a substitute for having done it.
You have built the checks, not only passed them. You have set up CI, tests or release gates for a team that ships many times a day, and you can tell us which checks earned their place and which ones you deleted.
You are fluent with AI coding tools and you do not trust them. You direct Claude Code or similar every day, you verify what it tells you, and you can explain why a plausible AI-written fix is wrong.

ActiveProspect is on a mission to make consent-based marketing the best channel for online customer acquisition. We provide marketers the products they need to acquire qualified customers at scale. LeadConduit, our real-time lead processing and routing platform, connects lead sellers and buyers and checks consent, data quality, and delivery rules on every lead.
Job Summary
You own customer and business outcomes, not tickets. You work like a forward-deployed engineer: you belong to the LeadConduit team, and you contribute to projects, initiatives, and pods where the problem is, deliver your work across the full stack (Vue/Nuxt and React/Next.js on the frontend, Node.js and TypeScript services on AWS), and improve processes for delivery in future projects. The technical bar is high, but coding ability is only the starting point. What sets this role apart is judgment: knowing the smallest thing worth shipping, when to drop your own idea, and when AI output is good enough versus when to override it. On LeadConduit, that work splits evenly between two areas: keeping today's platform fast and reliable for the customers who run their business on it, and building the next-generation platform, including a new real-time engine for ping/post, call tracking, and buyer optimization.
You'll move between the LeadConduit team and the initiatives you deploy into, shipping early, talking to customers, and deciding fast.
Responsibilities

- Own outcomes end-to-end, wherever you're assigned. Frame the problem, design it, ship it, own the metric. Distill to the cheapest version that works. Prototype in days.

- Work across today's LeadConduit and the next-generation platform. Improve the current product (flows, integrations, reporting) and help build the new real-time engine (field mapping, ping/post, call tracking, buyer optimization).

- Stay close to customers. Shadow sales and support, talk with lead buyers and sellers, join advisory conversations, and let customer reality drive technical decisions. Propose what to build, defer, and drop.

- Own your domain and share it. Its interfaces, reliability, performance, and security, including on-call for the systems you own. Consent, TCPA compliance, and PII handling are central to customer trust. Bring patterns, tooling, and hard-won context back to the wider org rather than hoarding them.

- Build and scale both the product surface and the platform beneath it. Ship responsive, accessible interfaces with a strong UI/UX eye (Vue/Nuxt today, React/Next.js for the new platform), back them with Node.js and TypeScript services and APIs, and keep the real-time, multi-tenant lead and call processing engine reliable and fast as volume grows.

- Architect AI-driven leverage. Build AI-assisted workflows that hold up, evolve the team's practices as tooling changes (Cursor, Claude Code, and whatever comes next), and look for product wins AI unlocks (smarter routing, anomaly detection on lead flow, AI-built integrations, and more).

- Make every team you work with stronger. Mentor on judgment and product sense, not just syntax. Write decision memos and ADRs. Enable Product and Design to self-serve.

Qualifications and Skills

- A track record of shipping something end-to-end that you cared about and owning the outcome, not just the code.

- Product judgment: pushing back on a bad spec, proposing the cheapest experiment, descoping, and collaborating with Product to suggest solutions rather than waiting for a fully specified ticket.

- Comfort embedding with unfamiliar teams and codebases, getting productive fast, and leaving them better than you found them.

- Deep full-stack expertise: React/Next.js and Vue/Nuxt (component lifecycle, state management, rendering optimization), JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern CSS on the frontend; Node.js and TypeScript services, RESTful APIs, and low-latency, high-volume asynchronous data handling on the backend.

- Cloud and real-time systems depth: AWS core services (Lambda, EC2, S3, DynamoDB, API Gateway) and event-driven, queue-based processing (SQS, SNS, Kafka, or similar) to deliver multi-tenant, real-time products reliably at scale.

- A strong UI/UX eye: you turn wireframes, mockups, and ambiguous requirements into intuitive, accessible, user-centric journeys.

- Strong systems design judgment in ambiguous contexts, and a security mindset aligned with sensitive consumer data and compliance.

- Lead generation or performance marketing experience is a strong plus: ping/post, lead routing and distribution, call tracking, or TCPA and consent rules.

- Fluency building your own AI-assisted workflows and reading AI output critically. Daily use of AI-native tools (Cursor, Claude Code) and precise prompting across OpenAI and Claude models, with the judgment to know when to trust output, how to review it for hidden bugs and security issues, and when to override it.

- Clear written and verbal communication. Mentorship experience. 5-10% travel.

How It Works
You'll report to an Engineering Manager who owns several teams and stays out of their daily flow. As you embed, you'll often act as the player-coach Tech Lead, owning technical direction while the EM owns delivery health and stakeholder alignment across the group.
Success looks like movement in a user or business metric your team owns, high-value work deliberately not built, decisions made fast, and teams that move faster after you've worked with them, not just while you're there.
